profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer III at Boston Scientific
profile.summary:
I am an Embedded Software Engineer at Boston Scientific focused on developing firmware for medical devices in regulated, safety-critical environments.

I earned my background in computer science at the University of Southern California, where I developed a strong foundation in software and embedded systems. This led me to pursue a career at the intersection of software, hardware, and healthcare.

I’m particularly interested in advancing technologies that improve system reliability, enhance performance, and ultimately contribute to better patient outcomes.

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Currently, I am leading a research project with several undergraduate students that aims to develop machine learning for Eye Fundus Imaging. Currently, we are in the algorithm development stage for preprocessing algorithms to normalize contrast between fundus images. We are also pursuing development methods for building a stable U-Net architecture. 

Previously I was aiding in the software development of radiation therapy decision support web application that assists physicians in targeting head and neck tumors. Here, I verified and tested components and parsing algorithms of the software architecture of the program in MATLAB.

company.name: USC Viterbi School of Engineering, Image Processing and Informatics Lab

positions.title: Research Intern
positions.description:
Developed Statistical Algorithms in MATLAB to analyze clusters of emerin protein image data

Implemented MATLAB code that utilized high process computation (parallel computing) for efficient analysis

Integrate new software architecture that allowed for usage of large image files in analysis

Increased the efficiency of former computational analysis methods in the lab by developing efficient software
